profile.name: Consumer Price Index
profile.what: Headline and core consumer inflation, month on month and year on year. Released 13:30 UK (08:30 ET).
profile.who: Bureau of Labor Statistics, monthly, usually mid-month
profile.why_gold: The most reliable single driver of Fed expectations, and therefore of gold. A hot print lifts real yields and the dollar and knocks gold; a cool one does the reverse.
profile.watch: Core m/m is what the market trades - headline is noisier because of energy. A 0.1pp surprise against forecast is enough to move the metal.
profile.gotchas: Gold's first move is sometimes reversed within the hour if the internals (shelter, supercore) contradict the headline.

profile.what: Michigan's household survey, released in preliminary and revised form at 15:00 UK.
profile.why_gold: The sentiment number is minor. The inflation-expectations component attached to it is not.
profile.watch: The 1-year and 5-10 year inflation expectations. The Fed watches the long-run figure closely, so a jump there is a genuine rate signal.
profile.gotchas: Small sample, frequently revised, and prone to reflecting petrol prices more than anything else.
